She reports that he has been experiencing abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, and fatigue consistently during the past year. expected.explanation_footer:
This patient with right lower abdominal pain, watery diarrhea, fatigue, anemia, and noncaseating granulomas on histology has Crohn disease . Crohn disease is a type of inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any portion of the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly the terminal ileum. Since the terminal ileum is the site of vitamin B 12 absorption, Crohn disease can lead to vitamin B 12 deficiency and present with macrocytic anemia, as seen in this patient. Unlike most other vitamins, vitamin B 12 has a large reserve stored mainly in the liver . Because of this storage capacity, it can take years for patients to clinically become vitamin B 12 deficient, even after the intake of vitamin B 12 decreases or the absorption is impaired. Thus, dietary deficiency is a rare cause vitamin B 12 deficiency (although it may be possible in long-term vegans). Vitamin B 12 deficiency most commonly occurs due to pernicious anemia (autoimmune destruction of parietal cells and intrinsic factor deficiency). It also occurs due to pancreatic insufficiency and damage to the terminal ileum from diseases that affect the terminal ileum (eg, Crohn disease or Diphyllobothrium latum infection). Treatment involves supplementation with vitamin B 12 either orally or through intramuscular injections.
